description:
Hi! I'm a B.Tech Information Technology student with a strong interest in Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, software development, and innovative technology solutions. I enjoy exploring real-world problems and developing AI-powered applications that turn complex data into meaningful insights.

For NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, I'm working on TerraEcho AI — Multisensory Earth Change Intelligence & Evidence-Based Decision Engine.
summary:
TerraEcho AI is a multisensory Earth observation and change intelligence platform designed to transform Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite data into understandable, evidence-based insights. It addresses the Dancing with the SARs challenge by analysing radar observations from different dates to identify changes on Earth's surface, even when optical imagery is limited by cloud cover or darkness.

The platform combines TerraShift for SAR-based change detection, Earth Change Fingerprints for structured change representation, and Historical Change Memory for comparing current observations with past patterns. Its Spectral Verification Matrix organizes supporting and conflicting evidence, while Eco-Pulse converts selected radar features into audio to provide an alternative way to explore detected changes. An evidence-grounded AI interpretation module explains observed changes, possible causes, and uncertainty. The platform also provides interactive geospatial visualizations and investigation reports for technical experts and communities.

TerraEcho AI is important because detecting environmental and surface changes is only the first step. Understanding the evidence, comparing historical patterns, communicating uncertainty, and supporting informed human decisions can make satellite observations more useful for environmental monitoring and Earth science investigations.
details:
1. What does it do or how does it work?

Answer:TerraEcho AI is a multisensory geospatial intelligence platform that transforms complex Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) observations (such as NASA-ISRO NISAR data) into structured, evidence-supported Earth-change intelligence.

How it works:

  • Detect (TerraShift): It processes SAR acquisitions to identify and segment surface changes (e.g., flooding, vegetation disturbance, or land deformation).
  • Fingerprint: It bundles each change into a structured Earth Change Fingerprint tracking spatial, radar ($\sigma^0$ decibels, polarization), temporal, and quality signatures.
  • Verify & Compare: It checks historical memory for seasonal recurrence and opens a Spectral Verification Matrix to show raw decibel shifts and Z-score anomalies against historical baselines.
  • Experience & Interpret: Users can explore data visually on an interactive map or sonify radar parameters into ambient soundscapes using Eco-Pulse (Web Audio API). An AI reasoning engine then ranks candidate explanations while explicitly surfacing uncertainty and missing data.
  • Act: It exports a structured Human-Reviewed Investigation Brief via a Dual-Audience Gateway (Expert GIS Mode vs. Community StoryMap Mode).

2. What benefits does it have?

Answer:

  • Lowers the SAR Complexity Barrier: Translates dense orbital radar physics into intuitive visual, numerical, and auditory formats for non-specialists.
  • Eliminates Black-Box AI Risk: Provides absolute scientific transparency through the Spectral Verification Matrix and explicit missing-evidence flags, ensuring users never confuse model guesses with confirmed physical causes.
  • Multi-Sensory Exploration: Introduces data sonification (Eco-Pulse), allowing analysts to perceive temporal variation and spatial texture through sound.
  • Dual-Audience Agility: Instantly bridges the gap between high-level GIS analysts (GeoJSON/STAC outputs) and local community stakeholders (plain-language StoryMaps).

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Answer: TerraEcho AI is designed as a rigorous decision-support and investigation tool for environmental analysts, researchers, and local planning groups. Its intended impacts are:

  • Accelerating Environmental Response: Helping stakeholders quickly prioritize which areas of surface change warrant urgent human investigation.
  • Improving Open-Science Transparency: Making NASA Earth observation data more accessible without sacrificing scientific credibility or overstating causal certainty.
  • Empowering Communities: Bridging the gap between orbital satellite missions and local communities by converting complex remote sensing insights into actionable, human-reviewed briefs.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use to develop your project?

Answer:

  • Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS (Dark Mode Design System), Deck.gl & MapLibre GL JS (Geospatial Rendering), Native Web Audio API (Eco-Pulse Sonification).
  • Backend & Geospatial Processing: Python 3.11, FastAPI, Rasterio, GDAL, NumPy, Pandas, Scikit-learn, PostGIS.
  • Data Sources & Standards: NASA Earth data STAC APIs, Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFFs (COGs), NISAR proxy data cubes, and Sentinel-1 L1 GRD/SLC products.

5. How is your project creative?

Answer: While 95% of hackathon teams submit standard map viewers with basic image split-sliders, TerraEcho AI introduces true multi-sensory and conceptual creativity:

  • The Earth Change Fingerprint: Moving away from binary raster masks to a multi-variable vector identity for every detected spatial anomaly.
  • Eco-Pulse Sonification: Translating radar backscatter intensity, spatial entropy, and coherence into real-time audio synthesis, letting users hear the structural stability of an ecosystem change.
  • Humble, Guardrailed AI: Designing an AI layer that actively searches for conflicting evidence and reports missing data rather than hallucinating definitive physical causes.

6. What factors did your team consider?

Answer:

  • Scientific Boundaries & Integrity: We strictly separated measured observations, derived features, and model interpretations, ensuring we never claimed arbitrary image pairs yield uncalibrated millimeter-level InSAR displacement.
  • Hackathon Feasibility & Demo Stability: Rather than risking a live, crash-prone backend pipeline, we structured our architecture around pre-cached Cloud Optimized GeoTIFFs (COGs) and structured JSON matrices to guarantee a 100% stable, lightning-fast demonstration.
  • Actionability vs. Caution: We designed the system as a decision-support platform that generates investigation briefs for human review, explicitly avoiding automated public emergency warnings or unsupported causal declarations.
